outcome: pregnant women's beliefs about the mode of delivery (behavioral beliefs, normative beliefs, control beliefs)
cohort: The participants were 36 pregnant women with a mean age of 27.8 years recruited from public hospitals in Tehran, Iran.
finding: The study found that while women generally preferred vaginal delivery, they expressed concerns related to pain, fears, loss of control, and health issues, categorized into behavioral, normative, and control beliefs.
mod_finding: Despite positive beliefs regarding vaginal delivery, participants indicated concerns related to loss of control and fear.
